lede: The most consequential thing on the calendar this week is Tuesday's joint P&Z and HARC special meeting, where the two commissions will hash out Land Use Code and Design Guideline amendments required to bring Telluride into compliance with the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code — language that then goes straight to Town Council for a final vote. Thursday brings two more substantive meetings: the Telluride Hospital District board takes up mill levy considerations tied to the push for a new facility, and P&Z holds a work session on the Shandoka Lot Redevelopment Project, the major Town-owned site that's been generating real conversation. Plenty of summer programming fills out the week, from the Yoga Festival to the Oak Street Park SummerSHOW Series kicking off Thursday.

notable.stake: Commission recommends Land Use Code changes for wildfire compliance; Council decides next.
Board discusses mill levy — the tax mechanism funding the hospital and new facility push.
Early public shaping of Shandoka Lot redevelopment before formal Land Use Code review begins.
